definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.S.Point
definitions.gloss: The type of finite lists of pairs (b, n) with b in K and n a natural number, such that every b is nonzero, every n is at least 1, and the n's add up to i.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.IsOmegaLeb
definitions.gloss: A proposition about a measure lam on lieU P Q. It states that lam is an additive Haar measure. It also states that the product measure lam × lam, pushed forward by the map sending (a, b) to the array of entries of the complex matrix a + i·b, equals the standard volume measure.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.UpqT.mat
definitions.gloss: A function that sends an element g of UpqT P Q, which is the group Upq P Q, to its underlying complex (P + Q) by (P + Q) matrix.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.ballU
definitions.gloss: The set of matrices X in lieU P Q for which the sum over all entries i, j of the absolute values ‖X i j‖ is less than r.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.lieU
definitions.gloss: The real vector subspace of complex (P + Q) by (P + Q) matrices X satisfying Xᴴ J + J X = 0. Here Xᴴ is the conjugate transpose and J = Jpq P Q is the block diagonal matrix with the identity in the first P coordinates and minus the identity in the last Q. The remaining lines prove that this set contains zero and is closed under addition and real scalar multiplication.

definitions.name: Formalism.UG.Upq
definitions.gloss: The subgroup of invertible complex (p + q) by (p + q) matrices given by UJ applied to complex conjugation and Jpq p q. It consists of the matrices g with cT(g) J g = J, where cT conjugates every entry and then takes the transpose, and J is the block diagonal matrix with entries 1 and −1.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.Rsum
definitions.gloss: A function that sends a family Nu of HLat data indexed by a finite type Words to the natural number given by the sum over u of dU Nu u.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.dU
definitions.gloss: A function that sends a family Nu of HLat data and an index u to the natural number that the code calls (Nu u).rank.

definitions.name: Formalism.HermitianLatticesTheory.dual
definitions.gloss: A function that takes a sesquilinear form h on the K-vector space V and an R-submodule L of V and returns hdual h L. This is the R-submodule of vectors x such that h y x lies in the image of R in K for every y in L.

definitions.name: Formalism.HC.HostDer
definitions.gloss: A proposition about a datum H of type HostRaw φ, stated as a list of thirty conditions. Among other things they say that H.art is surjective, that H.E is a CM field of degree 4 · φ.ord with a subfield H.F of degree 2 · φ.ord fixed by H.conj, that H.cmType is a CM type of size 2 · φ.ord, and they describe Frobenius elements, inertia groups and decomposition groups at primes of H.E through H.art and congruences modulo H.condN. The remaining conditions concern splitting of primes in H.K, the values of H.etaF, the different ideal with a unimodularity property, the discriminant of H.E being the square of that of H.F, bounds on H.rd such as 4 · φ.ord ≤ H.rd squared, and roots of unity having norm 1 to H.K.

definitions.name: Formalism.HC.HostRaw
definitions.gloss: A record type with twenty-six fields, depending on a Frame φ. It holds natural numbers q, d and QS with HostHyp q d (q and d prime, q ≡ 3 mod 8, d ≡ 7 mod 16, and the Jacobi symbol of −d at q equal to 1), with 2 ≤ φ.e, with QS > 0 and divisible by 2^(φ.e + 2), with QS coprime to q·d, and with the Jacobi symbol of −d equal to 1 at every odd prime dividing QS. It also holds a Galois number field E with a group isomorphism gal from its automorphism group to φ.GG, a square root sqd of −d in E, an embedding of E into the cyclotomic field of level QS·q·d with a primitive root, and a homomorphism art from the units modulo QS·q·d to φ.GG with five compatibility conditions.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.Loc.K0
definitions.gloss: For a finite extension K of ℚ_[l] inside Om l, the intermediate field given by the intersection of K with MaximalUnramifiedExtension l. That second field is the one generated over ℚ_[l] by the roots of unity of order prime to l.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.LocRings
definitions.gloss: A record type with ten fields, depending on a prime l. It holds two types B and BdR with commutative ring structures, algebra structures on B over ℚ_[l] and over MaximalUnramifiedExtension l that are compatible, and algebra structures on BdR over Om l and over ℚ_[l] that are compatible.

definitions.name: Formalism.WeaklyAdmissibleFiltrations.PeriodData
definitions.gloss: A record type with thirty-two fields, over a group G, fields Qp ⊆ K₀ ⊆ K and rings B and BdR with compatible algebra structures. It holds a prime p, finite-dimensionality of K₀ and K over Qp, a bijective automorphism σ of K₀, actions of G on B and on BdR with invariants K₀ and K, an injective σ-semilinear Frobenius φ on B that commutes with G, and an injective G-equivariant map ι from B to BdR. It further holds a decreasing, exhaustive, separated, multiplicative and G-stable filtration Fil of BdR indexed by ℤ with 1 in Fil 0, a character χ from G to the units of Qp, a unit t of B with g·t = χ(g)·t and φ t = p·t and ι t in Fil 1 but not in Fil 2, and the property that every b with φ b = b and ι b in Fil 0 comes from Qp.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.OC
definitions.gloss: For a prime p, the type of elements of the subring PadicComplexInt p of the Mathlib library.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Ainf
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a commutative ring R in which p is not a unit, the ring of p-typical Witt vectors with entries in Tilt p R, which is the Mathlib ring PreTilt R p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Bcris
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete commutative ring R in which p is not a unit, the localization of the ring BcrisPlus p R at its submonoid BcrisPlus.periods p R.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdR
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete commutative ring R in which p is not a unit, the fraction ring of BdRPlus p R.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdRPlus
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete commutative ring R in which p is not a unit, the adic completion of the ring AinfInv p R with respect to the ideal AinfInv.kerTheta p R. Here AinfInv p R is Ainf p R with p inverted, and AinfInv.kerTheta p R is the kernel of AinfInv.theta.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdR.fil
definitions.gloss: For an integer i, the BdRPlus-submodule of BdR p R obtained by dividing filNat p R at the positive part of i by filNat p R at the positive part of −i. Here filNat n is the image in BdR of BdRPlus.fil n, and the quotient I / J of submodules consists of the elements x with x·J contained in I.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.Acris
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the type Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris taken at the prime l and the ring OC l, which is the ring PadicComplexInt l. By that definition it is the adic completion, with respect to the ideal generated by l, of the ring AcrisZero built from OC l.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.Acris0
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the subalgebra acrisZero l (OC l) of AinfP l over Ainf l. It is the Ainf-subalgebra of AinfInv generated by the elements AinfInv.gamma n applied to the image of x, for every natural number n and every x in Ainf with Ainf.theta x equal to 0.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.AinfP
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the type AinfInv l (OC l). It is the localization of Ainf l (OC l), the Witt vectors of the tilt of OC l, away from the element l.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.a0B
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is a ring homomorphism from the subalgebra Acris0 l to Bcris l, defined to be UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.a0B l. That map is the structure map from AcrisZero into Acris followed by the structure map from Acris into Bcris.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.ev
definitions.gloss: For a prime l and a natural number n, this is the ring homomorphism from BdRp l to the quotient of AinfP l by the n-th power of the ideal kerP l. It is BdRPlus.eval at OC l and n, which takes an element of the adic completion to its level n component.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.pD
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is a ring homomorphism from AinfP l to BdR l, defined as UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.pD l. That map is the structure map from AinfP into BdRp followed by the structure map from BdRp into BdR.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris
definitions.gloss: Let p be a prime and R a commutative ring in which p is not a unit and which is adically complete for the ideal generated by p. This is the type given by the adic completion of the ring AcrisZero p R with respect to the ideal generated by p.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.Fl
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is an abbreviation for the type Tilt l (OC l). That type is the Mathlib type PreTilt of the ring OC l at l.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.tm
definitions.gloss: For a prime l and an element x of Fl l, this is the element of Ainf l given by the Teichmuller representative WittVector.teichmuller l x.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdRPlus.log
definitions.gloss: Given an element u of BdRPlus p R together with a proof that theta p R u equals 1, this is the element of BdRPlus p R obtained by applying adicLog for the ideal AinfInv.kerTheta p R to u. The hypothesis that adicLog needs is derived from this proof through a result that the code calls theta_eq_one_iff, whose body the file does not show.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.aB
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the ring homomorphism from Ainf l to Bcris l obtained by composing the structure map from Ainf l into Acris l with the structure map from Acris l into Bcris l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.zB
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the ring homomorphism from the l-adic integers to Bcris l obtained by composing the structure map from the l-adic integers into Acris l with the structure map from Acris l into Bcris l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.zD
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the ring homomorphism from the l-adic integers to BdR l. It first applies zP l, the structure map into AinfP l, and then pD l.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdRPlus.thetaC
definitions.gloss: Let C be a complete normed field of characteristic zero in which the norm of p is less than 1, and let O be a valuation subring of C for which IsUnitBall holds, so that O is the set of elements of norm at most 1. This is the ring homomorphism from BdRPlus p O to C that applies theta p O, which lands in the localization of O away from p, and then the ring isomorphism IsUnitBall.awayEquiv from that localization onto C.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.Gq
definitions.gloss: For a prime p, this is an abbreviation for the type of field automorphisms of PadicAlgCl p that fix the p-adic numbers.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.σO
definitions.gloss: For an element g of Gq p, this is the ring endomorphism of OC p by which g acts. It is obtained from the multiplicative semiring action of Gq p on OC p through MulSemiringAction.toRingHom.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Bcris.map
definitions.gloss: Given an injective ring homomorphism f from R to S, this is the ring homomorphism from Bcris p R to Bcris p S. It is built with Bcris.lift from BcrisPlus.map p f followed by the structure map into Bcris p S. Bcris.lift needs a proof that the image of Acris.logTeich of each primitive element of the Tate module is a unit, and this proof uses results that the code calls BcrisPlus.map_algebraMap, Acris.map_logTeich, isUnit_logTeich and IsPrimitive.map, whose bodies the file does not show.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.σD
definitions.gloss: For a prime l and an element g of Gq l, this is the ring endomorphism of BdR l by which g acts. It is obtained from the multiplicative semiring action of Gq l on BdR l through MulSemiringAction.toRingHom.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Bcris.frob
definitions.gloss: This is the ring endomorphism of Bcris p R built with Bcris.lift from BcrisPlus.frob p R followed by the structure map into Bcris p R. Bcris.lift needs a proof that the image of Acris.logTeich of each primitive element is a unit, and the proof writes that image as p times a unit. It uses results that the code calls BcrisPlus.frob_algebraMap, Acris.frob_logTeich, isUnit_p and isUnit_logTeich, whose bodies the file does not show.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.rhoVec
definitions.gloss: For a natural number N and an index i in Fin N, this is the rational number ((N - 1) / 2) - i.

definitions.name: Formalism.ConjugateSelfDual.Inertia
definitions.gloss: For a valuation subring A of the field Omega, which is an algebra over the number field F, this is a set of F-automorphisms sigma of Omega. A sigma is in the set when it lies in the decomposition subgroup of A and, for every x whose valuation is at most 1, the valuation of sigma x - x is less than 1.

definitions.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Above
definitions.gloss: For a number field F and a prime l, this is the set of height one primes v of the ring of integers of F whose ideal contains the integer l.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.GS
definitions.gloss: For a set S of height one primes of the ring of integers of the number field F, this is the quotient of the group G F Omega of F-automorphisms of Omega by the subgroup NS Omega S. That subgroup is the topological closure of the normal closure of the union of the sets Inertia A, over all primes v outside S and all valuation subrings A that lie over v in the sense of IsPlaceOver.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.toGS
definitions.gloss: This is the quotient group homomorphism QuotientGroup.mk' from G F Omega onto GS Omega S, taken with respect to the normal subgroup NS Omega S.

definitions.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Sha
definitions.gloss: For an LData record D at a prime l and an integer e, this is a submodule, over the l-adic integers, of H1 of the representation qzTw D e. It is Sha1 for the family locFam D.S D.A, which is the intersection of the kernels of the restriction maps on H1 along the maps from the groups Dec of the valuation subrings D.A v into GS. The continuity of these maps is supplied by a result that the code calls continuous_locFam, whose body the file does not show.

definitions.name: Formalism.CyclotomicNorms.Exc
definitions.gloss: For natural numbers g, d and ℓ, this is the proposition that ℓ is prime and that g^d is less than ℓ^(4 * v), where v is the ℓ-adic valuation of g^d - 1.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.HGrp
definitions.gloss: For a natural number e, this is the quotient of the unit group of the integers modulo 2^(e + 2) by the subgroup generated by -1.

definitions.name: Formalism.HC.Idx
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n, this is the type Fin n, whose elements are the natural numbers less than n.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.stdH
definitions.gloss: Take a field E with a star operation, a natural number N and two vectors x and y in E^N. This is the element of E given by the sum over i of star(x i) * y i.

definitions.name: Formalism.HermitianLatticesTheory.IsCMUnram
definitions.gloss: For a number field K with a star operation, this is the proposition made of three conditions. K is totally complex, and every ring homomorphism phi from K to the complex numbers sends star a to the complex conjugate of phi a. Also, for every maximal ideal P of the ring of integers of K there are integers theta and t in that ring such that t equals star theta in K and theta - t is not in P.

definitions.name: Formalism.HermitianLatticesTheory.vecAt
definitions.gloss: Take a basis b, indexed by a finite type, of a vector space V over the number field K, an infinite place v of K and a vector x in V. This is the complex vector whose i-th entry is the image of the i-th coordinate of x in the basis b under the embedding of K attached to v.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.G.HidaSetting
definitions.gloss: This is a proposition-valued record with 15 fields about natural numbers p and n', discrete valuation rings W and O, fields Qq and Kf, maps iota, sigma and j, and an element w of O. The fields say that p is a prime with 5 ≤ p and that n' is even with 2 ≤ n', that Qq and Kf are the fraction fields of W and O, that p is irreducible in W, that W modulo p has p^n' elements, and that W is p-adically complete. They also say that sigma takes each x of W to x^p + p * y for some y in W, that sigma^n' = 1, that iota agrees with j on W, that j is finite, that O is complete for its maximal ideal, and that w^2 = p.
second_errors: B says the record has 17 fields, but the Lean text of HidaSetting lists 15 fields, from prime to w_sq.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.G.IsDominant
definitions.gloss: For a function lam0 that gives, for each s in Fin n', an integer-valued function on Fin (m + 1), this is the proposition that for every s the function lam0 s is antitone, which means non-increasing.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.rankIso
definitions.gloss: For a list P of Part records over A.CG, this is the natural number obtained by summing a * d over all the entries of P.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.isoInf
definitions.gloss: For a list P of Part records over A.CG and a ring homomorphism tau from H.E to the complex numbers, this is a multiset of complex numbers. For each part p in P and each k from 0 to p.d - 1, it adds the number ((p.d - 1) / 2) - k to every element of the multiset A.infG p.π tau. It then adds all of these multisets together.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.ubc
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n and a multiset α of complex numbers, this is the multiset sum of α and the multiset of the inverses of the elements of α. When n is odd, the singleton {1} is also added, and when n is even nothing more is added.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.spehLoc
definitions.gloss: For a part p over A.CG and a place w in PlE H, this is an element of A.LP w built by a right fold over k from 0 to p.d - 1, starting from A.lpZero w. At each step it uses A.lpSum to add A.lpTw (A.locG p.π w) ((p.d - 1) / 2 - k), where the number is taken as a real number, to the accumulated value.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.Kf
definitions.gloss: For an index i in N.Loc, this is the type FractionRing (N.O i), the fraction field of the ring N.O i.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.galPol
definitions.gloss: For an element L of A.LP w at a place w, this is the complex polynomial given by the product of X - α over all elements α of the multiset A.frobEig L.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.iotaO
definitions.gloss: For an index i in N.Loc, this is a ring homomorphism from N.O i to the complex numbers. It sends N.O i into its fraction field, then applies A.iotaQ i into Qbar (N.l i), and then applies the ring isomorphism A.iotaQC i onto the complex numbers.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.N.IsInv
definitions.gloss: A proposition about a group homomorphism ρ from a group Γ into the invertible a by a matrices over a field k, and a subspace W of k^a. It says that for every g in Γ and every vector v in W, the matrix ρ(g) times v lies again in W, so W is stable under the representation.

definitions.name: Formalism.CyclotomicNorms.IsGood
definitions.gloss: A proposition about natural numbers N and a prime g, a family f of polynomials over ZMod g indexed by PP, and a family χ of units of ZMod g indexed by PP and J. It is the conjunction of six conditions. Each f v is monic of degree N with nonzero constant term and is squarefree. For every prime ℓ not in BB N g, two roots x and y of f v in rootsBar with the same primeToPart ℓ are equal. For every prime ℓ different from g, no root of f v has the same primeToPart ℓ as the image of χ v j in Fbar g. For every a with 1 ≤ a and 2a ≤ N some f v has no divisor of degree a. Finally some f v has an irreducible divisor q whose degree is prime, with N < 2 times that degree and that degree plus 3 at most N.

definitions.name: Formalism.MainNotions.S.Loc.SplitAt
definitions.gloss: A record type built from a valued field Fp, an Fp-algebra Ep, an algebra automorphism cj of Ep and a natural number ell. It has five fields. These are an algebra isomorphism e from Ep onto Fp × Fp that turns cj into swapping the two coordinates, together with an irreducible element q of the valuation ring of Fp whose image in Fp equals ell.

definitions.name: Formalism.BasicNotions.entries
definitions.gloss: A function that takes a complex square matrix Z whose rows and columns are indexed by the disjoint union of Fin P and Fin Q. It returns the function sending a pair of indices (i, j) to the entry Z i j.

definitions.name: Formalism.UG.Jpq
definitions.gloss: For natural numbers p and q, the complex block-diagonal matrix indexed by Fin p ⊕ Fin q whose upper-left block is the identity, whose lower-right block is minus the identity and whose off-diagonal blocks are zero.

definitions.name: Formalism.UG.UJ
definitions.gloss: For a ring endomorphism σ of a commutative ring A and a square matrix J over A, the subgroup of GL n A made of the invertible matrices g with cT σ g times J times g equal to J. The body includes proofs that this set contains the identity and is closed under products and inverses.

definitions.name: Formalism.E.hdual
definitions.gloss: For a form B on a K-vector space V that is conjugate-linear in the first variable and linear in the second, and an S-submodule L of V, this is the S-submodule of all x in V such that B y x lies in the image of S in K for every y in L. It is written as an infimum over y in L of preimages of the submodule spanned by 1.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.cmType
definitions.gloss: For elements ζ, a and b of a field L of characteristic zero and a natural number d, the set of ring homomorphisms φ from hostE ζ a b to the complex numbers with φ(bE ζ a b) equal to i times the square root of d.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.hcl
definitions.gloss: For a natural number e, the function that sends a unit u of ZMod (2^(e+2)) to its class in the quotient group HGrp e.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.HostHyp
definitions.gloss: A proposition about natural numbers q and d. It says that q and d are prime, that q % 8 = 3, that d % 16 = 7 and that the Jacobi symbol of -d over q equals 1.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Tilt
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a commutative ring R in which p is not a unit, the type Tilt is defined to be the Mathlib type PreTilt R p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BcrisPlus.periods
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete ring R in which p is not a unit, the submonoid of BcrisPlus p R generated by the images of Acris.logTeich ε under the canonical map from Acris p R, as ε runs over the elements of tateModule p R that satisfy IsPrimitive.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AinfInv
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a commutative ring R in which p is not a unit, the localization of Ainf p R obtained by inverting the element p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AinfInv.kerTheta
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete ring R in which p is not a unit, the ideal of AinfInv p R that is the kernel of the ring homomorphism AinfInv.theta p R.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdR.filNat
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n, the BdRPlus p R submodule of BdR p R obtained as the image of BdRPlus.fil p R n under the canonical algebra map from BdRPlus p R to BdR p R.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.acrisZero
definitions.gloss: The Ainf p R subalgebra of AinfInv p R generated by every element AinfInv.gamma n applied to the image of x, where n is a natural number and x is an element of Ainf p R with Ainf.theta p R x = 0.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.a0B
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the ring homomorphism from Acris0 l to Bcris l that composes the canonical map from AcrisZero l (PadicComplexInt l) into Acris l with the canonical map from Acris l into Bcris l.

definitions.name: Formalism.Per.kerP
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the ideal of AinfP l given by AinfInv.kerTheta for the ring OC l.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdRPlus.eval
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n, the ring homomorphism from BdRPlus p R onto the quotient of AinfInv p R by the n-th power of AinfInv.kerTheta p R. It is the level-n evaluation map of the adic completion.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.pD
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the ring homomorphism from AinfP l to BdR l that composes the canonical map from AinfP l into BdRp l with the canonical map from BdRp l into BdR l.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AcrisZero
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete ring R in which p is not a unit, the type of elements of the subalgebra acrisZero p R.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdRPlus.theta
definitions.gloss: The ring homomorphism from BdRPlus p R to the localization of R that inverts p. It first evaluates at level one of the adic completion, which gives the quotient of AinfInv p R by AinfInv.kerTheta p R, and then applies the map that AinfInv.theta p R induces on that quotient by its kernel.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.adicLog
definitions.gloss: For a commutative ℚ-algebra A, an ideal I and an element u of the I-adic completion whose level-one image equals 1, this is the element of the completion built by adicMk from the sequence whose n-th term is truncLog n applied to the level-n image of u - 1. The body includes a proof that these terms are compatible across levels.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.Acris
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the type Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris taken at l and the ring PadicComplexInt l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.Ainf
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the type Reformulated.AutPerF.Ainf taken at l and the ring PadicComplexInt l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.Bcris
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the type Reformulated.AutPerF.Bcris taken at l and the ring PadicComplexInt l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.BdR
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the type Reformulated.AutPerF.BdR taken at l and the ring PadicComplexInt l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.zP
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the canonical ring homomorphism from the l-adic integers ℤ_[l] into AinfP l.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.IsUnitBall
definitions.gloss: A property of a valuation subring O of a normed field C. It holds when every element x of C lies in O exactly when the norm of x is at most 1.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.IsUnitBall.awayEquiv
definitions.gloss: Suppose C has characteristic zero, O is the closed unit ball of C, p is nonzero and the norm of p is less than 1. Then this is the O-algebra isomorphism from the localization of O that inverts p onto C, given by the universal property of localization.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Bcris.lift
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism g from BcrisPlus p R to a commutative ring B that sends the image of Acris.logTeich ε to a unit for every primitive ε in tateModule p R, this is the ring homomorphism from Bcris p R to B that extends g. It comes from the universal property of localization at BcrisPlus.periods p R, and the body proves by induction on the closure that every element of that submonoid goes to a unit.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BcrisPlus
definitions.gloss: For a prime p and a p-adically complete ring R in which p is not a unit, the localization of Acris p R obtained by inverting p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BcrisPlus.map
definitions.gloss: For a ring homomorphism f from R to S, the ring homomorphism from BcrisPlus p R to BcrisPlus p S induced by Acris.map p f followed by the canonical map into BcrisPlus p S. It is built with lift, using a fact that the code calls isUnit_p to show that p goes to a unit.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.Gq
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, the type of field automorphisms of PadicAlgCl l that fix ℚ_[l].

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BcrisPlus.frob
definitions.gloss: The ring endomorphism of BcrisPlus p R induced by Acris.frob p R followed by the canonical map into BcrisPlus p R. It is built with lift, using a fact that the code calls isUnit_p to show that p goes to a unit.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.NS
definitions.gloss: For a number field F, an F-algebra field Ω and a set S of nonzero primes of the ring of integers of F, the subgroup of G F Ω defined as the topological closure of the normal closure of the union of all Inertia A. The union runs over primes v outside S and over valuation subrings A of Ω for which IsPlaceOver A v holds.

definitions.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.qzTw
definitions.gloss: For data D of type LData F Ω l and an integer e, the ℤ_[l]-linear representation of GS Ω on QZ l through scalars, given by scalRep applied to the character D.chi raised to the power -e.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.H1
definitions.gloss: For a representation rho of a topological group G on a topological R-module M, the quotient of Z1 rho by the part of B1 rho that lies in Z1 rho. In other words it is the first cohomology, cocycles modulo coboundaries.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.Sha1
definitions.gloss: For a representation rho and a family of continuous group homomorphisms phi i from groups D i into G, the R-submodule of H1 rho given by the intersection over all i of the kernels of the restriction maps resH1 rho (phi i).

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.locFam
definitions.gloss: For a finite set S of nonzero primes of the ring of integers of F and a choice of a valuation subring Av v of Ω for each v in S, the family that gives for each v in S the group homomorphism locHom from Dec (Av v) to GS Ω S.

definitions.name: Formalism.CyclotomicNorms.primeToPart
definitions.gloss: A function that takes a natural number ℓ and an element x of a monoid M and returns x raised to a certain power. Let a be the exponent of ℓ in the prime factorization of the order of x, and let m be the order of x divided by ℓ^a. The exponent is ℓ^a times the natural-number representative of the inverse of ℓ^a in the integers modulo m.
first_errors: A says that ℓ^a is the exact power of ℓ that divides the order of x, but the Lean text uses ℓ ^ (orderOf x).factorization ℓ with ℓ any natural number, and for a composite ℓ the factorization exponent is 0 even when a positive power of ℓ divides the order.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.bE
definitions.gloss: For elements ζ, a, b of a field L of characteristic zero, this is the element b regarded as an element of the intermediate field hostE ζ a b. The proof that b lies in that field is a fact the code calls b_mem.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.hostE
definitions.gloss: For elements ζ, a, b of a field L that is an algebra over ℚ, this is the intermediate field between ℚ and L given as the join (compositum) of E0 a b and F1 ζ. In other words it is the smallest subfield containing ℚ(a, b) and ℚ(ζ + ζ⁻¹).

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris.logTeich
definitions.gloss: For an element η of tateModule p R, this is the element of Acris p R obtained by applying the logarithm Acris.log to the Teichmüller lift of the underlying element of η. The condition that θ of that lift equals 1 comes from η lying in the kernel of untilting, through a fact the code calls Ainf.theta_teich.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.IsPrimitive
definitions.gloss: A proposition about an element ε of tateModule p R. It says that if you apply the inverse of the p-th power Frobenius of Tilt p R to the underlying element of ε and then untilt, the result in R is not equal to 1.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.tateModule
definitions.gloss: The submonoid of the multiplicative monoid of Tilt p R made of the elements whose untilt in R equals 1. Formally it is the multiplicative kernel of the monoid map PreTilt.untilt. Here p is a prime and R is a commutative ring in which p is not a unit and which is p-adically complete.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AinfInv.theta
definitions.gloss: The ring homomorphism from AinfInv p R, the ring Ainf p R with p inverted, to the localization of R away from p. It is defined as Mathlib's fontaineThetaInvertP for R and p, which is Fontaine's map θ after inverting p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BdRPlus.fil
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n, this is the ideal of BdRPlus p R equal to the n-th power of the kernel of the ring homomorphism theta from BdRPlus p R to R with p inverted. These ideals form the filtration indexed by n.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Ainf.theta
definitions.gloss: The ring homomorphism from Ainf p R to R given by Mathlib's Fontaine map WittVector.fontaineTheta for R and p. Here R is p-adically complete and p is not a unit in R.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AinfInv.gamma
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n and an element x of AinfInv p R, this function returns x^n multiplied by the rational number 1/n!. It is the n-th divided power of x.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.Acris0
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the subalgebra acrisZero l of AinfP l over Ainf l, taken with R equal to PadicComplexInt l.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.AinfP
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the type AinfInv l (PadicComplexInt l). It is the ring Ainf with l inverted, built over that ring.

definitions.name: UpperTheory.Ring.Comp.BdRp
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the type BdRPlus l (PadicComplexInt l), the completion ring BdRPlus built over that ring.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.adicMk
definitions.gloss: Given an ideal I of a commutative ring A and a family x of elements x n of A/I^n, one for each n, that are compatible (for m ≤ n the natural map A/I^n → A/I^m sends x n to x m), this builds the corresponding element of the I-adic completion of A. It does this by lifting to the completion the polynomial-evaluation homomorphisms that send the variable X to x n and then evaluating at X.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.truncLog
definitions.gloss: For a natural number N and an element x of a commutative ℚ-algebra B, this is the truncated logarithm series, the sum over k from 0 to N − 1 of ((−1)^k/(k + 1)) times x^(k+1). It is the first N terms of the series for log(1 + x).

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris.map
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism f from R to S, this is the ring homomorphism from Acris p R to Acris p S. It is obtained by applying Acris.extend to the induced map AcrisZero.map p f.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.BcrisPlus.lift
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism g from Acris p R to a commutative ring B in which p is a unit, this is the unique extension of g to a ring homomorphism from BcrisPlus p R, which is Acris p R with p inverted, to B. It uses the universal property of localization away from p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris.frob
definitions.gloss: The ring endomorphism of Acris p R obtained by applying Acris.extend to the Frobenius endomorphism AcrisZero.frob p R of AcrisZero p R.

definitions.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.QZ
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the quotient of the l-adic numbers ℚ_l by the submodule ZlSub l, the image of the l-adic integers ℤ_l. In other words it is ℚ_l/ℤ_l.

definitions.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.scalRep
definitions.gloss: Given a commutative ring R, a group Γ, an R-module M and a group homomorphism ψ from Γ to the units of R, this is the representation of Γ on M in which each g acts as multiplication by the scalar ψ(g). The proofs check that the identity acts trivially and that the action respects products.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.B1
definitions.gloss: For a representation ρ of a topological group G on a topological R-module M, this is the submodule of all functions from G to M given by the image of the linear map d0 ρ. It consists of the functions g ↦ ρ(g)m − m for m in M, the 1-coboundaries.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.Z1
definitions.gloss: For a representation ρ of a topological group G on a topological R-module M, this is the submodule of functions f from G to M that are continuous and satisfy f(gh) = f(g) + ρ(g)(f(h)) for all g and h in G. These are the continuous 1-cocycles, and the proofs check closure under zero, addition and scalar multiplication.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.resH1
definitions.gloss: Given a representation ρ of G and a continuous group homomorphism φ from H to G, this is the R-linear restriction map from H1 ρ to H1 of the representation ρ composed with φ. It is induced on quotients by restrictCocycles1, which is well defined because a coboundary pulls back to a coboundary, using a fact the code calls mem_coboundaries1.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.locHom
definitions.gloss: For a valuation subring A of a field Ω over a number field F and a set S of primes of the ring of integers of F, this is the group homomorphism from the decomposition subgroup Dec A to GS Ω S. It is obtained by including Dec A into the Galois group and then applying the quotient map toGS.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.E0
definitions.gloss: For elements a and b of a field L of characteristic zero, this is the intermediate field ℚ(a, b) generated over ℚ by a and b.

definitions.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.F1
definitions.gloss: For an element ζ of a field L of characteristic zero, this is the intermediate field ℚ(ζ + ζ⁻¹) generated over ℚ by ζ + ζ⁻¹.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris.log
definitions.gloss: For an element u of Ainf p R with θ(u) = 1, this is the element of Acris p R, the p-adic completion of AcrisZero p R, whose image modulo p^n is the class of logPartial (p^n) u for each n. The compatibility of these classes is a fact the code calls logPartial_sub_mem.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Ainf.teich
definitions.gloss: The multiplicative monoid homomorphism from Tilt p R to Ainf p R, which is the ring of Witt vectors over Tilt p R. It is given by the Teichmüller lift WittVector.teichmuller p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris.extend
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism g from AcrisZero p R to AcrisZero p S, this is the induced ring homomorphism between their p-adic completions Acris p R and Acris p S. It is built with adicMap, using a fact the code calls span_natCast_le_comap to show that g sends the ideal generated by p into the ideal generated by p.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AcrisZero.map
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism f from R to S, this is the ring homomorphism from AcrisZero p R to AcrisZero p S obtained by applying AcrisZero.extend to Ainf.map p f. The required condition on divided powers is a fact the code calls gamma_map_mem.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AcrisZero.frob
definitions.gloss: The ring endomorphism of AcrisZero p R obtained by applying AcrisZero.extend to the Witt vector Frobenius Ainf.frob p R. The required condition on divided powers is a fact the code calls gamma_frob_mem.

definitions.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.ZlSub
definitions.gloss: For a prime l, this is the ℤ_l-submodule of ℚ_l given by the image of the natural algebra map from the l-adic integers ℤ_l into the l-adic numbers ℚ_l.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.d0
definitions.gloss: For a representation ρ of G on an R-module M, this is the R-linear map from M to the functions from G to M that sends m to the function g ↦ ρ(g)m − m.

definitions.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.restrictCocycles1
definitions.gloss: Given a representation ρ of G and a continuous group homomorphism φ from H to G, this is the R-linear map from Z1 ρ to Z1 of ρ composed with φ that sends a cocycle f to the composite f ∘ φ. The proof checks that f ∘ φ is continuous and still satisfies the cocycle identity.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Acris.logPartial
definitions.gloss: For a natural number N and an element u of Ainf p R with θ(u) = 1, this is the element of AcrisZero p R equal to the sum over k from 0 to N − 1 of (−1)^k k! times the (k+1)-th divided power AcrisZero.gamma (k + 1) (u − 1). Since k! times the (k+1)-th divided power is (u − 1)^(k+1)/(k + 1), this is a partial sum of the logarithm series of u.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.adicMap
definitions.gloss: Given commutative rings A and B, ideals I of A and J of B, and a ring homomorphism f from A to B with I contained in the preimage of J, this is the induced ring homomorphism from the I-adic completion of A to the J-adic completion of B. At each level n it reduces modulo I^n and applies the map A/I^n → B/J^n induced by f, using a fact the code calls pow_le_comap_pow.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AcrisZero.extend
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism ψ from Ainf p R to Ainf p S such that for every n and every x with θ(x) = 0 the n-th divided power of the image of ψ(x) lies in acrisZero p S, this is the ring homomorphism from AcrisZero p R to AcrisZero p S. It is the restriction of AinfInv.extend p ψ, and the fact that it lands in AcrisZero p S is one the code calls extend_mem.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Ainf.map
definitions.gloss: Given a ring homomorphism f from R to S, this is the ring homomorphism from Ainf p R to Ainf p S obtained by applying the Witt vector functor WittVector.map to the induced map Tilt.map p f between the tilts.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Ainf.frob
definitions.gloss: The ring endomorphism of Ainf p R, the Witt vectors over Tilt p R, given by the Witt vector Frobenius WittVector.frobenius.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AcrisZero.gamma
definitions.gloss: For a natural number n and an element x of Ainf p R with θ(x) = 0, this is the n-th divided power of the image of x in AinfInv p R, which is x^n/n!. It is regarded as an element of AcrisZero p R, since it is one of the generators of that subalgebra.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.AinfInv.extend
definitions.gloss: Fix a prime p and commutative rings R and S in which p is not a unit. This function takes a ring homomorphism f from Ainf p R to Ainf p S and returns a ring homomorphism from AinfInv p R to AinfInv p S, where AinfInv p R is the localization of Ainf p R away from p (that is, with p inverted). It is built with the universal property of that localization, applied to f followed by the canonical map from Ainf p S into AinfInv p S, using a fact the code calls isUnit_p to show that p becomes a unit in AinfInv p S.

definitions.name: Reformulated.AutPerF.Tilt.map
definitions.gloss: Fix a prime p and commutative rings R and S in which p is not a unit. This function takes a ring homomorphism f from R to S and returns a ring homomorphism from Tilt p R to Tilt p S, where Tilt p R is the Mathlib object PreTilt R p. First f induces a map between the quotients by the ideals generated by p, which is well defined by a fact the code calls span_natCast_le_comap. That quotient map is then passed to the perfections with Perfection.map.
